comment: Pairs not worth attempting again without new information. A null solver blocks the problem for every integration, which is right when the limit is in the reference itself. generation.coverage drops these from the work queue; add an entry when you block a pair, with the evidence that justifies it.

blockers.detail: Z3 could not prove the minimum ruler length for any of the three instances at 180s. A performance limit of this solver on this problem, not a reference or contract fault, so it is blocked for z3_python only. A materially better encoding would justify retrying.

The instance field Qualified is a ragged array: one variable-length list of qualified workers per task. MiniZinc's data interface binds a list of lists as a rectangular 2D array, so the runner fails with 'non-uniform array literal' before solving, whatever the model says. Reshaping the field inside run.py would be the problem-specific converter the integration's skill rules out, so this is an integration limit rather than a modelling one.

Each row of the instance field movies mixes a string title with an integer start and end. MiniZinc's data interface binds a list of lists as a rectangular array of one element type and refuses with "non-uniform array literal. Expected `string' but got `int'", whatever the model says. Same class of obstacle as the ragged Qualified field of covering_opl.

The declared output is the whole ten-digit pandigital number, which is at most 9876543210 and so exceeds the 32-bit FlatZinc integer range Gecode accepts: the parser rejects the model with "The literal '9999999999' of the type int is out of range (-2147483646..2147483646)" before solving. Any faithful model has to represent that value, so this is an integration limit rather than a modelling one. A solver with a wider integer type would not hit it.

The licence bundled with the gurobipy wheel allows 2000 variables and 2000 constraints. The order-7 instance (json:4) needs all 49 cells distinct over 1..49: a one-hot encoding is 2401 binaries, and a pairwise one is 1176 disequalities, each two constraints. The one-hot model passes the four smaller instances and is refused on json:4. A full Gurobi licence would not hit this.

The licence bundled with the gurobipy wheel allows 2000 variables and 2000 constraints. For n = 13 and 15 the output has 26 and 35 triples; stating that two triples share at most one element takes one AND variable per triple pair and element (4225 and 8925), or one per triple and element pair (2028 and 3675). The AND-variable model passes n = 7 and 9 and is refused on n = 13 (json:2). A full Gurobi licence would not hit this.

The CPLEX Community Edition in the cplex wheel allows 1000 variables and 1000 constraints. The order-7 instance (json:4) needs all 49 cells distinct over 1..49: 2401 one-hot binaries, or 1176 pairwise disequalities, each one variable and two constraints in docplex. The one-hot model was refused on json:4 at the gurobipy integration's larger limit of 2000; the full CPLEX would not hit this.

The CPLEX Community Edition in the cplex wheel allows 1000 variables and 1000 constraints. For n = 13 and 15, stating that two of the 26 or 35 triples share at most one element takes 4225 and 8925 AND variables pairwise, or 2028 and 3675 per triple and element pair. The AND-variable model was refused on n = 13 at the gurobipy integration's larger limit of 2000; the full CPLEX would not hit this.

Choco proves the makespan optimum only on the embedded example and the 3-job ragged instance (2 of 5 instances); ft06, la01 and the 6x3 instance each run past the 180 s limit. Two encodings behave the same: pairwise disjunctions on each machine and cumulative constraints of capacity 1. The model was evaluated and accepted on those two instances but not retained. A search strategy or an encoding with stronger disjunctive propagation would justify retrying.
